(a) we propose a method to efficiently distill adversarial attacks into neural models that can be used to attack models in black box settings; (b) we demonstrate that the distilled model generalizes well to examples not seen during training; and (c) we show that our approach is effective in black box settings, and that the distilled model outperforms other baselines in terms of accuracy and attack efficiency

We show that the knowledge of a white-box attack can be distilled into a black-box model, which can be used to generate efficient and effective adversarial attacks on neural models.
